claim: which ring carbon of the toluidine rings carries the methyl
locus_a: SI p18/p19, CBB21 and CBB1 IUPAC names: '...methylene)bis(3-methyl-4,1-phenylene))bis(ethylazanediyl)...'
locus_b: SI pp43-50, every CBBZ IUPAC name: '...methylene)bis(2-methyl-4,1-phenylene))bis(ethylazanediyl)...'
what_we_emitted: methyl ORTHO to the central methine, META to the nitrogen, in both series
why: Under any single locant convention the two divalent 'x-methyl-4,1-phenylene' forms contradict each other. The MONOVALENT prefixes in CBB6/7/12/13/14/20 do not, and in a monovalent prefix position 1 is unambiguously the attachment: '(4-(...amino)-2-methylphenyl)' on the central methine and '-3-methylphenyl)(ethyl)amino' on the nitrogen both give ortho-to-methine. Supplementary Figure 1 and Figure 3 DRAW it that way (renders/crop_core.png, renders/crop_fig3.png), and both series descend from the same intermediate I2, 3-((ethyl(m-tolyl)amino)methyl)benzenesulfonic acid, whose N-alkyl-m-toluidine is attacked para to the nitrogen (C4), ortho to the C3 methyl. Every candidate is an isomer, so no mass check can see this.

locus_a: SI p26: 'HRMS of CBB12 calculated for C85H130N9O7S2+'
what_we_emitted: C85H127N9O7S2 neutral, i.e. C85H128N9O7S2+ as the cation
why: The two statements in that one sentence disagree by 2.0156 Da. C85H128N9O7S2+ is 1450.9373 to four decimals -- the SI's own printed m/z and its own found value. C85H130 would be 1452.953. The homolog arithmetic agrees independently: CBB6 (bis-palmitoyl) minus C8H16 is exactly 1563.0625 - 112.1252 = 1450.9373. So the m/z is right and the formula STRING has a two-hydrogen typo.

locus_a: SI p30: 'HRMS of CBB17 calculated for C65H82F6N9O7S3+'
what_we_emitted: C65H81F6N9O7S2 neutral, i.e. S2 not S3
why: CBB17 is CBB21 bis-trifluoroacetylated and trifluoroacetic acid contains no sulfur, so the only sulfurs are the dye's two sulfonamides. C65H82F6N9O7S2+ reproduces the printed 1278.5678 to 0.0001; adding a third sulfur puts it 31.972 too high. The S3 is almost certainly carried over from CBB18 in the same paragraph, which legitimately has three (two sulfonamides plus the methionine of CPP5).

locus_a: SI p23: 'HRMS calculated for C95H150N9O7S23+' (the formula)
what_we_emitted: the structure the FORMULA describes: CBB6 bis-palmitoyl with both linker nitrogens quaternised, C95H149N9O7S2 as a dication
why: UNRESOLVED, and the only one of the three. C95H150N9O7S2 3+ computes to 531.0361, i.e. the printed m/z is 0.3345 high, which is 1.0035 Da over a charge of 3. Our structure matches the formula exactly, and the homolog spacing confirms it independently: CBB4 and CBB7 differ by exactly C12, so their 3+ m/z values must differ by 48.0000, and 579.0361 - 48.0000 = 531.0361. What is uncomfortable is that the FOUND value tracks the printed calculated one to 0.4 ppm. We did not pick a structure to make the m/z agree. See DECISIONS.md D-3.

locus_a: SI p29 synthesis heading: 'the tert-butyloxycarbonyl (boc)-protected CPP5 peptide (KLVPM)'
locus_b: main text Results: 'the C-terminus of a cell-penetrating peptide (CPP5, sequence KLPVM)'
what_we_emitted: NO SMILES for CBB18 or CBB19. Both candidates are in 03_enumerated.csv; the value rows carry confidence=low and structure_assumed=1
why: KLVPM and KLPVM are permutations of the same five residues, so they have identical molecular formulas and identical exact masses. Both pass the HRMS check identically -- which is the demonstration, not the resolution: mass cannot see connectivity. Nothing in the paper breaks the tie. See DECISIONS.md D-1.

locus_a: SI Fig 3 block table (SI p4): 'Z10 (L14, L14, 1, 1, K7)', where L14 is Hexadecyl
locus_b: SI p49-50: the reagent 'dodecyl 1-azido-21-(3-(dodecyloxy)-3-oxopropyl)-...-oate' and the product name '21-(3-(dodecyloxy)-3-oxopropyl)-...-azaheptatriacontyl'
why: Three independent statements say dodecyl: the reagent's name, the product's name, and the HRMS. C92H134N7O17S2+ reproduces the printed 1672.9273 to 0.0001 on dodecyl; dihexadecyl would be C100H150N7O17S2+, 112.1 higher. The figure's table cell is the outlier. Declared as an expected mismatch in paper_library.DRAWN_Z_EXPECTED_MISMATCH so stage07 P11 reports it rather than hiding it.

claim: the locants in CBB20's retinamide name
locus_b: the same paragraph names the reagent: 'all-trans-retinoic acid (50 mg, 166 umol)', which is 3,7-dimethyl-9-(2,6,6-trimethylcyclohex-1-en-1-yl)nona-2,4,6,8-tetraenoic acid
what_we_emitted: retinoyl, i.e. the all-trans-retinoic acid connectivity
why: The two methyl sets are positional isomers, so the HRMS formula C101H136N9O7S2+ cannot separate them -- it passes either way. The reagent weighing does separate them from the mass side only in the sense of confirming retinoic acid itself: 50 mg / 166 umol = 301.2, and retinoic acid is 300.44 (stage07 P2). An amide made from all-trans-retinoic acid is retinamide, so the named reagent governs and the amide name's locants are a name-generator artefact.

claim: what the '+/- SD' after a mean means
locus_a: Figs 2c and 4c: CBB3 '3.9 +/- 0.4', CBB11 '28.6 +/- 0.7', CBB19 '22.4 +/- 0.6' all reproduce only on the SAMPLE sd (ddof=1)
locus_b: Fig 6a: TAS '45.8 +/- 12.9', Lipo1 '227 +/- 69' and four more reproduce only on the POPULATION sd (ddof=0); the sample sds are 14.87 and 75.55
what_we_emitted: the per-replicate values themselves, plus both sds in 07_qc.json; no sd is emitted as the value
why: Two conventions in one paper, both labelled 'mean +/- SD'. The ratios are exactly sqrt((n-1)/n) -- 0.8660 for the n=4 groups and 0.9133 for the n=6 groups -- so this is not rounding. It changes no emitted value but it would change any error bar a reader re-derived, and anyone pooling the two figures' uncertainties would be mixing conventions.

claim: the delivery efficiency of a given compound
locus_a: Fig 2c (flow cytometry): CBB14 = 58.21% RFP conversion; Fig 4c (flow): CBB11 = 28.61% eGFP/mCherry
what_we_emitted: four separate assay blocks, Fig2c / Fig2d / Fig4c / Fig4d, each row carrying its own method field; NOT pooled
why: Same compound, same cargo, same cell line, same ratio, same lab -- and the two instruments disagree by 0.55x in one direction and 1.86x in the other. Not an error (the legends state which instrument each panel used) but a value conflict that pooling would silently average away. It is also a within-lab, same-chemistry, instrument-only concordance point in its own right.

claim: the protonation state of the CBBZ dye core
locus_a: SI Fig 3 draws the product as the N-protonated cation with both sulfonic acids as HO-SO2-
locus_b: every CBBZ IUPAC name: '...imino)cyclohexa-2,5-dien-1-ylidene...dibenzenesulfonic acid', and the HRMS reported as [M+H]+ of a neutral
why: Connectivity is identical; only the proton differs. All ten CBBZ HRMS formulas and m/z values reproduce exactly on the neutral, so the names and the mass spectra agree with each other against the drawing. Recorded as expected_mismatch on the CBBZ0 C10 anchor rather than silently normalised.
